title: Add benchmark-lab mixed representative workload runners and reporting pipeline v51
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a new mixed-workload representative runner, updated profiling baselines, and a CI-driven reporting pipeline that uploads run artifacts and summary metrics to the benchmark dashboard. No runtime-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: The benchmark lab needs a compact mixed-workload runner that better represents production traffic patterns (concurrent short chat interactions + long completion batches) and an automated reporting pipeline that uploads per-run metrics and profiling baselines to the benchmark dashboard. This PR adds: 1) a new runners/mixed_runner harness that composes existing chat and completion workload generators into a single representative workload; 2) profiling baselines (baseline configs + golden traces) for the mixed runner on common model shapes; 3) a CI reporting pipeline (benchmark-lab/reporting/pipeline.yaml) that runs scheduled benchmark jobs, collects flamegraphs/KV cache hit traces, computes summary metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec, memory), and uploads JSON summaries to the internal benchmark dashboard; 4) lightweight docs and a quickstart for running locally. Implementation notes: the mixed runner reuses the workload abstraction used by representative_runners, adds a small work-stealing scheduler to emulate concurrent short-lived sessions, and emits structured metrics compatible with the reporting pipeline. For profiling baselines we store representative trace artifacts under benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/v51 and include checksums so CI can detect regressions. The reporting pipeline is designed to be idempotent and tolerant of transient failures (backoff + retries) and stores artifacts in the same S3 bucket used by previous pipeline versions. Checklist: - [x] Mixed runner implementation + unit tests - [x] Profiling baselines added and checksum-verified - [x] Reporting pipeline + CI job - [x] Docs/quickstart updated - [x] Reviewed and approved by perf and infra teams
